vectors.name: a-list-item-inside-a-refused-frontmatter-span-is-not-stamped
vectors.note: SPEC.md §5.3 (v1.11), the write refusal at child granularity. Lines 1 to 7 open with `---`, close at the first `---`, hold a blank line and a YAML-ish `title:` line, so §5.3 recognition rejects them as frontmatter while a frontmatter reader would take them as YAML. The list between them is a block of its own with two §5.5 items, and a writer mints nothing in the span: not the list, which starts there, and not either item. The container's refusal does not carry its items with it, because a child-capable writer checks each child on its own. Drop that check and a writer stamps `- ship the build` and `- tag the release` inside the YAML; the Python reference's backstop, which requires lines 1 to 7 to come out byte-identical, then refuses the whole write instead, so the body paragraph goes unstamped. Either way this vector fails. Pinned here for any child-capable core; the block-level half is core, in `spec/stamp.json`.

vectors.note: SPEC.md §9.2 tier 0 (v1.11): `P`'s stored prefix is the intro paragraph above it. After the edit a table whose own marker survives (`Q`, claimed) sits between the intro and `P`'s reworded list, and a slightly more reworded copy sits further down.
